questions.question: Backing a school bus is:

options.text: Strongly encouraged.
Strongly discouraged.
Only to be done in the morning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strongly discouraged.
questions.explanation: Backing a school bus is not recommended. Only back up if there is no other safe option. If you must back up, follow all safety rules.

questions.question: When parking in an offset back-left space, a driver should:

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back-left parking maneuver, first pull straight forward. Then back up to the left. Park your vehicle completely inside the parking space lines.

questions.question: When approaching a school bus stop, the bus driver should:

options.text: Not use their mirrors.
Approach the stop with caution.
Stop on the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the stop with caution.
questions.explanation: A school bus driver should always approach bus stops slowly and carefully.

questions.question: When boarding a school bus, students should:

options.text: Be in a single-file line.
Be in pairs.
Not use the handrail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be in a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Students should board the school bus slowly in a single-file line. For safety, students should hold the handrail while boarding.

questions.question: ABS helps you:

options.text: Lock up your wheels.
Keep your wheels from locking up.
Count the number of students boarding the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: Loading and unloading a bus:

options.text: Can be hazardous for passengers.
Should be supervised by someone other than the driver.
Should be done when refueling.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be hazardous for passengers.
questions.explanation: Passengers may trip when getting on or off a school bus. The driver should warn passengers to watch their step when leaving.

questions.question: When encountering a railroad crossing during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if the other vehicle is moving too slowly.
Change lanes while on the tracks.
Not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: When students board a bus, they should:

options.text: Sit in the back row first.
Sit in the back row only after all other seats are filled.
Be seated as far from the driver as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit in the back row only after all other seats are filled.
questions.explanation: Students should not sit in the back row unless the bus is full. Sitting toward the front of the bus is safer in a rear-end crash. Students with special needs should sit near the driver.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, you will receive points if you:

options.text: Pull up once.
Check your positioning.
Cross over exercise boundaries.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross over exercise boundaries.
questions.explanation: The examiner counts each time your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each crossing is an error and counts against your test score.

questions.question: When stopping to pick up students, park at least 10 feet away from them because:

options.text: You will have a good view of their movements.
It will be difficult to get any closer to the students.
Students should walk for exercise.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have a good view of their movements.
questions.explanation: When picking up passengers, park your bus with the front bumper at least 10 feet from the students. This distance is safest because students must walk to the bus, allowing the driver to watch them.

questions.question: Crossover mirrors help the driver see:

options.text: The danger zone in front of the bus.
The rear bumper.
The left side of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The danger zone in front of the bus.
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors help the driver see the danger zone directly in front of a school bus. They also show danger zones on the left and right sides of the bus, from the front to the service door.

questions.question: ABS allows you to:

options.text: Drive faster.
Drive less carefully.
Keep control on slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep control on slippery roads.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents the brakes from locking up on slippery surfaces. This helps you maintain control when you brake hard on wet or icy roads. Drive and brake a vehicle with ABS the same way as one without ABS.

questions.question: If a school bus stalls on railroad tracks:

options.text: Students should stay on the bus.
Students should be evacuated near the bus.
Students should be evacuated and moved far from the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students should be evacuated and moved far from the bus.
questions.explanation: If a bus stalls on railroad tracks, evacuate everyone immediately. Move students far away from the bus at an angle in the direction of any oncoming train to avoid flying debris.

questions.question: At a passive railroad crossing, who decides if you can proceed:

options.text: The driver.
A control device.
The vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: A passive crossing has no traffic control devices. The driver alone decides whether it is safe to cross the tracks.

questions.question: When asked to make a turn during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Skip the turn signal since you were told to turn.
Check traffic only on your right.
Check traffic in all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: When making a turn during the driving test, check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.

questions.question: Before evacuating a bus due to a hazard, a driver should:

options.text: Ask the students if they want to leave.
Tell the dispatcher about the situation.
Take their time deciding if evacuation is needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the dispatcher about the situation.
questions.explanation: If there is time, contact your dispatcher before evacuating. Explain the situation. However, the decision to evacuate must be made quickly if needed.

questions.question: When approaching a bus stop, the driver should:

options.text: Not use the mirrors.
Approach slowly and carefully.
Drive fast and stop suddenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: School bus drivers should approach stops slowly and carefully.

questions.question: If there is a fire on a school bus, students:

options.text: Must be evacuated.
Should stay on the bus in an unaffected area.
Should stay in their seats.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be evacuated.
questions.explanation: If there is a fire or threat of fire on a school bus, you must evacuate all students immediately.

questions.question: When students exit at school, a driver should:

options.text: Turn off the engine and secure the bus.
Leave the key in the ignition when leaving the driver's seat.
Read while students unload.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine and secure the bus.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine to secure the bus when students unload. Remove the key from the ignition if you leave the driver's seat. Supervise the unloading process.

questions.question: Before a trip, make sure that:

options.text: The brake pedal sticks.
The gas pedal is loose.
The pedal surfaces are grooved and not worn smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pedal surfaces are grooved and not worn smooth.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check that nothing blocks the pedals. Make sure pedals work properly and have grooved surfaces for good grip.
